result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility crosswalks and traffic signals but requires pedestrians to cross a wide roadway with four travel lanes and embedded trolley tracks. While sidewalks are present and in good condition, the lack of a median refuge or curb extensions increases exposure to vehicle traffic.

hazards.name: Trolley tracks
hazards.description: Embedded tracks in the roadway can be a tripping hazard for pedestrians and a slip hazard for cyclists.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway within the intersection.

hazards.name: Long crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a refuge island, increasing exposure time.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main thoroughfare.

hazards.name: Sight line obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the intersection may obscure pedestrians from the view of approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image along the curb.

interventions.title: Curb extensions
interventions.description: Shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian refuge island
interventions.description: Provide a safe waiting area in the middle of the wide roadway to allow for two-stage crossing.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the crosswalk to improve sight lines for both drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The image depicts an urban intersection with mixed-use buildings and streetcar tracks embedded in the roadway. While basic infrastructure like sidewalks, curb ramps, and pedestrian signals are present, safety is compromised by a large vehicle obstructing sightlines and the presence of tracks in the pavement.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Large Vehicle
hazards.description: A large black pickup truck is positioned across the tracks, significantly blocking sightlines between pedestrians at the corner and oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground, blocking the intersection view

hazards.name: Streetcar Tracks
hazards.description: Metal tracks in the roadway create a slip and trip hazard for pedestrians, particularly where the surrounding pavement is cracked or uneven.
hazards.location_in_image: Running through the center of the roadway

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The transverse crosswalk markings are faded, reducing their visibility to approaching motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground across the side street

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Implement parking and standing restrictions near the intersection to ensure clear sightlines for pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Upgrade faded transverse markings to high-visibility continental (ladder) style markings to improve driver yielding rates.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and physically prevent vehicles from blocking the pedestrian path at the corner.

result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure including continuous sidewalks, marked crosswalks, and pedestrian signals. While functional, the environment lacks advanced safety features like curb extensions or high-visibility crosswalk markings to further protect vulnerable road users.

hazards.name: Standard crosswalk markings
hazards.description: The parallel line crosswalk markings are less visible to approaching motorists compared to high-visibility continental designs.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main and side streets

hazards.name: Wide corner radius
hazards.description: The corner geometry allows for higher-speed vehicle turns, increasing the risk of conflict with pedestrians in the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Right foreground corner

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and reduce vehicle turning speeds.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Upgrade existing parallel line markings to continental or ladder-style markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval
interventions.description: Adjust signal timing to provide pedestrians with a 3-7 second head start before vehicles receive a green light.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a sidewalk with significant physical obstructions from utility poles and a lack of basic crossing infrastructure. Although a traffic signal is present, there are no marked crosswalks or pedestrian signals, and the roadway contains trolley tracks that increase the risk of trips or falls.

hazards.name: Sidewalk obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located in the center of the pedestrian walkway, narrowing the effective path.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground sidewalk

hazards.name: Unmarked crossing at signalized intersection
hazards.description: The intersection lacks marked crosswalks despite having a traffic signal, increasing exposure risk.
hazards.location_in_image: Center roadway at the intersection

hazards.name: Trolley tracks
hazards.description: Embedded tracks in the roadway create a tripping hazard and a slipping risk for pedestrians and cyclists.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway

interventions.title: High-visibility crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Pedestrian countdown signals
interventions.description: Add dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear crossing intervals.

interventions.title: Sidewalk repair and clearance
interventions.description: Repair cracked pavement and relocate or consolidate utility poles to provide a clear, accessible walking path.
